editorial:
Imagine losing your child in a terrible accident and then watching your partner lose their grip on reality. That is the nightmare Michael and Allison are living. Allison is so heartbroken that she acts like their daughter, Jody, is still in the house. She makes Michael play along, like bringing breakfast to an empty room. It feels heavy and sad at first, but the vibe shifts quickly when a live-in therapist arrives to help. What starts as a plan to heal the family turns into a total trap, and you will feel the tension rise as the house becomes a place of fear rather than a home.

The acting is great because it makes the grief feel real before the crazy stuff happens. While the movie starts a bit slow, the twists in the second half really pick up the pace. If you love psychological thrillers where you cannot trust anyone, you will dig this. You should definitely try to find the 4K Blu-ray to add to your physical collection for the best picture quality, or just rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night. It is a solid pick for a rainy weekend when you want something that keeps you guessing.
endingExplained: You find out that the therapist is not there to help at all. She is actually a manipulator who wants to take over the family and control them for her own gain. She uses Allison's mental state to drive a wedge between the couple. In the end, the truth comes out in a violent clash. Michael finally sees the danger and has to fight back to save his wife and reclaim his life from the intruder.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves twisty thrillers and scary home settings.
